main_text.p: & Ecclesiasticarum rerum statu, (nisi sit nefas statum dicere, quæ mera ἀκα-ταστασία[?] sit, & perturbatissima rerum omnium confusio,) unus aliquis fortè melioris luti, & alter repertus fuerit, qui tristes Musas Musarumque quocunque in genere alumnos, maximè qui veræ & Christianæ Philosophiæ professores, spretos ubique & velut mundi retrimenta abjectos, curet alloquio aliquo, aut levamine so-lari. Si quid igitur (Deo Opt. Max. donante) posthac mihi in hoc genere scriptionis, hoc est, quod ad Mora-lem Theologiam pertineat, tentatum editúmque fuerit, sive id Latino idiomate fiat, sive (quod sentio ef-fe plerisque nostratium aliquanto optatius) vernaculo, quod aut in publicum utile, aut privato cuivis homini, ad vitam rectè instituendam, moresque ex Divinæ Legis & Evangelii præscripto efformandos, usui esse poterit: id tibi plurima ex parte acceptum ferri debere, & agnosco lubens, & libere profiteor; qui mihi

page.notes: The Greek word at the line end is uncertain (ἀκαταστασία). The left strip shows the neighbouring page's edge and was omitted. A small mark at the top left corner is printing or stain and was left out. The text is set in roman with italic words; no black letter occurs. The page carries no page number or running head.
